what_its_for: Sitagliptin is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by helping your body release more insulin after meals and reducing the amount of sugar your liver makes. It is used along with diet and exercise, and sometimes with other diabetes medicines.
how_to_take: Take sitagliptin by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The most common dose is 100 mg once a day. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose (50 mg or 25 mg once a day). Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store sitagliptin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar levels. Do not skip meals or change your diet drastically without talking to your doctor. Let all of your healthcare providers know you are taking this medicine before starting any new prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: severe pain in your stomach, back, or sides (could be a sign of pancreatitis); skin blisters, rash, or peeling (serious skin reactions); signs of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion (especially if taking with other diabetes medicines); signs of kidney problems such as less urination, swelling in your legs or feet; joint pain that is severe or unusual; or signs of an allergic reaction such as trouble breathing, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat.
when_it_works: Sitagliptin starts working within a few days, but it may take several weeks to see the full benefit on your blood sugar levels. Your doctor will check your HbA1c (a 3-month average blood sugar test) and other blood tests regularly to see how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your dose may need to be lowered if your kidneys do not work well. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Older adults (65 years and older): This medicine is generally safe for older adults, but kidney function should be monitored regularly. Pregnancy: It is not recommended to use this medicine during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, so you can discuss the safest options for you and your baby. Children: Sitagliptin is not approved for use in people under 18 years of age.
